A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, including complete Appendices A–H. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that all pages except the first-page arXiv stamp and page 7 are identical; the substantive revision concerns Theorem 5.3.

before.justification: v3 reports original symmetry assessments on QM9 and ModelNet40, synthetic point-cloud separation experiments, and GeoNGNN benchmark and chirality results in Appendices F and H.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Section 6, Tables 1–7, and the evaluations in Appendices F and H.

M1.justification: GeoNGNN's procedures, Definition 5.2's general geometric subgraph architecture, and Appendix H's GeoNGNN-C remain unchanged. The revised theorem assumption does not change the proposed algorithms or their implementations.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same QM9 and ModelNet40 symmetry assessments, synthetic separation cases, rMD17/MD22/3BPA/QM9 benchmarks, and chirality classification, enantiomer ranking, and binding-affinity tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within every comparison in Tables 1–7. Table 1 retains SchNet, DisGNN, DimeNet, SphereNet, GemNet, PaiNN, and MACE alongside GeoNGNN; Appendix H retains the same chirality baselines.

E3.justification: Experimental splits, preprocessing, metrics, cutoffs, and model configurations in Appendices C.3, G, and H.2 are unchanged. Theorem 5.3 revises a theoretical sufficient-depth assumption, not a reported experimental setting.

E4.justification: The noise-tolerance assessment in Section 6.1, subgraph-size sensitivity in Figure 6, efficiency analysis in Table 4, and temperature-shift evaluation in Table 5 are retained without modification.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains its standard deviations computed over three runs, and Table 7 retains the same uncertainty entries. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and reported findings are identical. For example, Table 1 retains 0% separation for SchNet and DisGNN and 100% for the other six models in both case groups; Tables 2–7 and Figures 2 and 6 are unchanged.

T1.justification: v3's Theorem 5.3 imports all Theorem 5.1 conditions, including GeoNGNN's Nin >= 5 and Nout >= 0. v4 instead requires general geometric subgraph depth greater than a node-count-independent constant C, retaining only the full-connectivity and whole-graph-subgraph conditions. This is a limited correction to the sufficient assumptions; the proof is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same DisGNN near-completeness claim and completeness contributions for GeoNGNN, geometric subgraph GNNs, DimeNet, GemNet, and SphereNet. The depth-assumption correction does not alter these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning expressiveness versus generalization, full-connectivity limitations, and sparse-graph open questions in Sections 5.4 and 7 and Appendix F are unchanged. No explanatory or limitations discussion accompanies the theorem correction.

D1.justification: Appendices G and H retain the same architectural details, hyperparameters, training procedures, hardware, training times, and evaluation instructions. No implementation or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. The theorem revision introduces no new attribution or novelty claim.

P1.justification: Theorem 5.3 receives a short rewrite making its depth condition explicit, and the first-page arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining prose, terminology, section order, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded theorem statement causes slight local spacing and text reflow on page 7, and the marginal arXiv stamp changes. All figures, tables, captions, and other page layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: The revised Theorem 5.3 better matches Appendix B.5's existing proof, which allows an additional layer for SV pooling, improving the precision of the sufficient-depth condition. The benefit is limited: Appendix B.5 still repeats the old theorem statement, and nearby prose still claims exactly the same conditions as GeoNGNN.
